notes: *do* moved from οὐ to διορύσσουσιν: rule 9 gives an inflected Greek verb its English auxiliary, rule 17 treats an auxiliary as part of the verb's unit rather than as a head, and no rule assigns do-support to a negator. The chapter's other three do-support renderings — 6:26 *do they reap*, 6:28 *do they spin*, 6:30 *doth … clothe* — all place it on the verb, so rule 24's habit settles the construction.
Both negatives are realized in English (*not*, *nor*), so neither rule 41 nor rule 59 empties one.
